precepts.label: Genesis 43:32
precepts.why:
“And Joseph was the governor over the land, and he it was that sold to all the people of the land: and Joseph’s brethren came, and bowed down themselves before him with their faces to the earth.” Our forefathers hated Joseph and sold him into slavery. He gained status in Egypt, Egypt got through the famine by his counsel, and now his brothers came to Egypt to buy food.

“And Joseph knew his brethren, but they knew not him.” If Joseph had been a German Jew, or from Holland, Ukraine or Poland, they would have known him: a white man in Egyptian clothes stands out among Egyptians, because the Egyptians are black. They could not recognize their brother because he was dressed in Egyptian garb, beard shaved, looking like an Egyptian. “for he spake unto them by an interpreter”: he acted the part, speaking Egyptian so they would not know him. Joseph passed for an African, a black man, just as Abraham, Isaac and Jacob were dark ancestors.

Then Genesis 43:32, at the meal: “And they set on for him by himself, and for them by themselves, and for the Egyptians, which did eat with him, by themselves: because the Egyptians might not eat bread with the Hebrews; for that is an abomination unto the Egyptians.” That is Jim Crow. The Hebrews sat over there and the Egyptians over here, because them sitting together was an abomination. Israel had its own land, Goshen, and Egypt was apart. It was still segregation, even though both were dark: same color, different nation.

The pictures shown from the history books said the same. The Egyptians are brown. The Israelites working in the granary under a taskmaster have afros. Pharaoh is black, and Tutankhamun is black. Nefertiti is black as hell, and the Nubians are black as hell. The sacrifice of Isaac in the mosaic of the Beth Alpha synagogue shows Abraham and Isaac as black. The sons of Ham, the Egyptians, Canaanites, Nubians and Libyans, are all dark; we fought the Canaanites in the land, and they are black too.

Moses passed for an Egyptian the same way. Jethro's daughters said, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. Moses married an Ethiopian woman, a daughter of Ham, and a Hamite would have known a white man was no Egyptian. Even Pharaoh's daughter knew the baby was a Hebrew only because he was circumcised, since both peoples were black.

precepts.label: Exodus 1:16-17
precepts.why:
Pharaoh’s crafty counsel had a plan behind it, and here it is: “When ye do the office of a midwife to the Hebrew women, and see them upon the stools; if it be a son, then ye shall kill him: but if it be a daughter, then she shall live.”

What they were hoping for was to run into Hebrew women who hated themselves and hated their people, so their plan could be executed. They were doing it by proxy of the midwives, hoping the midwives felt the way the rebellious Israelites felt coming out of Egypt: we miss the garlics, we miss the leeks, take us back, we like being a slave. They were hoping they loved their enemy and hated themselves.

“But the midwives feared God, and did not as the king of Egypt commanded them, but saved the men children alive.” That means the midwives loved their people. They feared God, and the way they showed it was that they loved their people.

The enemies of Israel have always capitalized off of our hatred of ourselves. What was commanded in Egypt is what abortion has evolved into: make the babies that come out of Israelite wombs vanish. Now the black mind has been so twisted and perverted that they do not even have to put out an edict that says kill the children. The black woman will do it herself, and she is already doing it by the millions. That is a genocide in itself.

That is why we must be the ones to correct this, to highlight it, illuminate it, and set the nation back in order: restore the love of ourselves and the fear of God, and show that the enemy hates us.

precepts.label: Exodus 1:8
precepts.why:
“Now there arose up a new king over Egypt, which knew not Joseph”. This new king set taskmasters over Israel to afflict them with burdens, and then went further: “And Pharaoh charged all his people, saying, Every son that is born ye shall cast into the river, and every daughter ye shall save alive”.

That is gator bait. They sacrificed our baby boys in the river to Sobek, the gator god. The white man did the exact same thing to us in the Florida Everglades: put our babies in a net, wait for the alligator to bite, pull the gator out and make shoes and bags out of him. Egypt did it to us first. They killed the males and kept the women alive, because the women do not produce the nation; the man does.

That decree is why Moses was hidden three months and laid in an ark of bulrushes by the river's brink, and why everything that follows was done in secret. When Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river in Exodus 2:5 and found the ark, she found one of the very sons her father had ordered cast into the river.

precepts.label: Numbers 12:1
precepts.why:
When Pharaoh's daughter opened the ark, “she had compassion on him, and said, This is one of the Hebrews’ children”. How did she know? He was circumcised. You never read about Moses getting circumcised; he was already cut, because some of our forefathers retained that custom from our fathers. Outside of that, she would not have known the difference, because Egyptians and Hebrews were both black.

Then Moses fled to Midian and helped the seven daughters of the priest of Midian at the well, and they told their father Reuel, “An Egyptian delivered us out of the hand of the shepherds”. What did they call Moses? An Egyptian. The same way Joseph's brothers took Joseph for an Egyptian. Reuel, Jethro, gave Moses Zipporah his daughter.

Numbers 12:1 shows what that family was: “And Miriam and Aaron spake against Moses because of the Ethiopian woman whom he had married: for he had married an Ethiopian woman”. She was Ethiopian, so Moses' father-in-law was an Ethiopian, a priest of Midian but not a Midianite. Ethiopians are children of Ham, Kushites, the family of the Egyptians. A Hamite would know a Hamite when he saw one, and they still took Moses for an Egyptian. If he had been a white man, they would have known he was no Egyptian.

Paul passed for one too: “Art not thou that Egyptian”, the chief captain asked, and Paul answered, “I am a man which am a Jew of Tarsus”. Moses passed for an Egyptian, Joseph passed for an Egyptian, Paul passed for an Egyptian. These are black people. That's the point.

Menstealers goes straight back to Exodus 21:16, stealing people for slavery. In Christ, a man who was a trafficker back then could repent. But if you are involved in child trafficking today, get out of that nonsense.

And that is our history. Loango Bay, where the Portuguese traders came, was on the old maps called the Jews' Bay, because the Jews were there. From that West Central African coast, Loango and Angola, nearly half of all the captives in the Atlantic slave trade were shipped to the Americas and the Caribbean. Menstealing is what was done to us, and the law says the man who did it should surely be put to death.

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:11
precepts.why:
“They ravished the women in Zion, and the maids in the cities of Judah.” They raped our women; they raped the Judahite sisters. This is not new. Whatever color the oppressor was, the nations all had the same habits, because judgment is like a ring: it recurs over and over again. Same game, different characters.

It is the curse of Deuteronomy 28:30: “Thou shalt betroth a wife, and another man shall lie with her”. In The Butler, the master takes the boy's mother from the cotton field; she cannot say no; she screams, and the father and everyone in the field stand there powerless, unable to do a thing. In The Birth of a Nation, a guest demands Hark's new wife Esther for the night, and the master allows it; she comes out in tears, and he cries, Where is God now? That racial anger is what drove Nat Turner to take the axe to the master. We were powerless to protect our wives and our children. And “thou shalt build an house, and thou shalt not dwell therein”: we built the house and never dwelt in it.

That trauma is the madness of verse 28: “The Lord shall smite thee with madness, and blindness, and astonishment of heart”. Coming off those ships we were smitten with madness. In 12 Years a Slave, Patsey, beaten until her back was ripped open for a piece of soap because she could not stand her own smell, begs Solomon Northup to hold her under the water until she is without life, and to bury her in a lonely place; she has no comfort in this life. You cannot expect reparations to fix that. Blindness is spiritual: some watching right now say Jesus and the Jews are white; they are gone. “And thou shalt grope at noonday, as the blind gropeth in darkness, and thou shalt not prosper in thy ways”, as a nation.

You millennials grew up thinking the white man is peaceful and loving and your friend. Malcolm X, Martin Luther King and our people of the 50s, 60s and 70s knew who the enemy was; after that we forgot and started saying the enemy is only a spiritual demon. They gave us Section 8, food stamps and Christianity, and we went back to sleep. So God is letting Trump and the administration behind him do evil, reverting the white man to his true nature, and JD Vance says they will no longer apologize for being white, so that we develop that racial anger again. That is why they want to remove this history from the museums and the schools. Let your children watch Roots, 12 Years a Slave, The Birth of a Nation, Amistad; the Holy Ghost brings all things to remembrance, and the scripture says what they did to our women in Zion.

That is what was told of the man brought to this side of the world. Then verse 34: “So that thou shalt be mad for the sight of thine eyes which thou shalt see.”

You are going to be mad. Your eyes are going to be mad for what you see: the oppression, all the evil taking place against your people. You see your wife being raped and you cannot do anything. You see your people being lynched and you cannot do anything. You are just angry. The curse prophesied that anger.

So if you see your people oppressed and going through these things, and you are not mad, not angry, something is not right. You have shut down. There must be racial anger. Being mad at the sight of the oppression of our people is not a sin to be ashamed of; it is what the scripture said the oppression would do to us, and it is the wise response to what our eyes have seen.

precepts.label: Lamentations 5:12
precepts.why:
“Princes are hanged up by their hand: the faces of elders were not honoured.” Princes hanged up means lynched. Young or old, it did not matter; you were hanged all the same.

That is what “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee” comes to. Hanging in doubt does mean you will wonder whether you live or die, worried day and night, in the hood, the ghetto and the slums, and further back in slavery and colonization: “In the morning thou shalt say, Would God it were even! and at even thou shalt say, Would God it were morning!” But it also means hanging. Lamentations 5 is the whole picture of the curse: “Our inheritance is turned to strangers, our houses to aliens”, the European, the East Indian and the Chinese man in Africa and Trinidad reaping our resources; “We have drunken our water for money; our wood is sold unto us”, which is colonization; “Servants have ruled over us”, those who were once our slaves.

The Spaniards hanged the Americans thirteen at a time and set them on fire. Without Sanctuary, a book of lynching photographs, shows it: 1935, which was yesterday; postcards of our fore mothers and fathers hanging from trees; a man burned to pieces, his hands and legs cut off and kept as souvenirs; a mother and son hanged from a bridge in 1901. White people today say, I didn't do that, that was my ancestors. But look at the postcards: children, fathers, mothers, women right in the middle, the whole family supporting it, children who grew up to be your lawyers, teachers, mayors and police officers.

Mary Turner, in 1918, grieving her husband Hayes Turner, lynched without a trial, threatened to have his killers punished. The next day she was hanged from a tree, burned, her womb cut open; the baby, a month shy of being born, cried on the ground, and a member of the white mob crushed its head with his foot; then they shot her full of holes. Now they say they are not apologizing anymore. In Queens in 1976 white children chased little black girls out of their neighborhood with rocks and dogs, calling them niggers, and those children are judges, lawyers and police officers now. This is war.

Hanging is nothing new; the Persians did it (1 Esdras 6:32), “out of his own house should a tree be taken, and he thereon be hanged”. Christ himself was lynched: “whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Peter called the cross a tree, wood, where he hung for hours. “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”: Christ went under the curse along with us. The King and his children were hanged. Princes are hanged up by their hand.

precepts.label: 2 Maccabees 6:10
precepts.why:
The Greeks did it too. Under Antiochus, 1 Maccabees 1:60-61: “they put to death certain women, that had caused their children to be circumcised.” “And they hanged the infants about their necks, and rifled their houses, and slew them that had circumcised them.” After they killed the mothers, they hung the circumcised babies from their dead mothers' necks and put them on display for the people to see. They lynched our babies on their mothers' necks. It is the same persecution recorded of the mothers who circumcised their children and were led about the city with the babes at their breasts.

Esau was so demonic and wicked that he ran around checking who was circumcised, running through our houses and killing anyone who circumcised a child. Who does that? Demons.

That is Deuteronomy 28:66: “thy life shall hang in doubt before thee; and thou shalt fear day and night, and shalt have none assurance of thy life”. Keeping the law of God, circumcising your child as the covenant commands, could cost a mother her life and her baby's. It is the same spirit that hanged our princes, burned our mothers and crushed our babies here in America. Same game, different characters: judgment is like a ring, recurring over and over.

Peter and the apostles answered, “We ought to obey God rather than men”, and the mothers of the Maccabees did so to the death. Christ was hanged on a tree too; the King and his children have all hung under the same curse, until the Lord says enough.

precepts.label: Psalms 137:3
precepts.why:
“For there they that carried us away captive required of us a song; and they that wasted us required of us mirth, saying, Sing us one of the songs of Zion.” “How shall we sing the Lord’s song in a strange land?” We read it right there in the history of the slave ships.

Deuteronomy 28:68 says “the Lord shall bring thee into Egypt again with ships”. What does Egypt represent? “I am the Lord thy God, which have brought thee out of the land of Egypt, out of the house of bondage.” Egypt is bondage. The Lord would bring us into bondage again, this time by way of ships; literal Egypt we would see no more again as a nation, and there we would be sold to our enemies for bondmen and bondwomen, slave men and slave women.

The Middle Passage, the Maafa, a massive disaster: for fifty days or more our people were packed in spaces as tight as coffins, a second platform barely twenty inches above the heads of those below, chained to the floor, lying in their own waste, amid rats that gnawed through wood and flesh, on floors covered with blood and excrement, where pregnant women gave birth and the living awoke chained to the dead. Tight packers crammed in as many as possible, reckoning the sales would offset the dead. The meal was horse beans pounded to a pulp with slabber sauce, once or twice a day, and a pint of water. Dumb negroes say it never happened and ask where the ships are: cargo ships carried spices and corn before us, carried us as cargo, and after slavery carried cargo again. Why get rid of them?

Then came the dancing of the slaves: the crew played the bagpipe or forced our ancestors to beat out a rhythm while they jumped about, ankles rubbed raw by the leg irons, to keep the human cargo in salable condition. That is Psalms 137:3: those who carried us away captive required of us mirth. At night the cries rose; an enslaved woman explained the howling came from having dreamt they were in their own country and waking in the hold of a slave ship. A strange land indeed.

Millions were carried from Africa to the West Indies, North and South America and Europe, from Luanda, from the Congo, from Loango, where the old maps mark the Jews; the buyers and sellers both knew they were selling outsiders, not the same people. Deuteronomy 28:68 and Psalms 137:3 were fulfilled on those ships.

A plant has its own melanin, chlorophyll, that gives it the green colour; deprive it of water and sunlight and it turns brown and withers, like the Jews here. They did it before, in the days of an evil king named Jehoram.

The Hamite, the Arab and the white man worked together removing us far from our border, and the land is parted today between the Israelis and the Arabs. That is why God will plead with the nations in the valley of Jehoshaphat for his people.

precepts.label: Galatians 2:4
precepts.why:
“I marvel that ye are so soon removed from him that called you into the grace of Christ unto another gospel: Which is not another”. It is not another because it is found in the law of Moses. “but there be some that trouble you, and would pervert the gospel of Christ.” They are the same men of Acts 15, who went out from us and troubled the churches. Paul says, if any man preach any other gospel, “let him be accursed”. Those men were running around joining the churches and causing confusion by infiltration, pushing a gospel we are no longer under: going back to sacrificing animals. That is another gospel.

Chapter 2 names them: “And that because of false brethren unawares brought in, who came in privily to spy out our liberty which we have in Christ Jesus, that they might bring us into bondage”. The liberty we have is that we no longer offer up animals. Christ died on the cross, and we are free from that burden. So Galatians 5 says “Stand fast therefore in the liberty wherewith Christ hath made us free, and be not entangled again with the yoke of bondage.” If animal sacrifice saves you, Christ died for nothing and you are fallen from grace. Yet “ye have been called unto liberty; only use not liberty for an occasion to the flesh”: do not use this freedom to do what you want and sin.

Likewise today, Christians will come in here and do the same thing: accept the identity, but not the theology, using the same book and the same Bible to push Christianity. That is the same infiltration in reverse. As John says, “They went out from us, but they were not of us”, and those who trouble you shall bear their judgment.

precepts.label: Acts 5:30
precepts.why:
Peter and the other apostles told our wicked elders, “We ought to obey God rather than men.” And then: “The God of our fathers raised up Jesus, whom ye slew and hanged on a tree.” Christ was lynched.

Why does Peter call it a tree? What is the cross made of? Wood. Hanging on the cross is hanging on a tree. He says it again in Acts 10:39: “whom they slew and hanged on a tree”. Some say he was hanged from an actual tree, but Thomas said, “Except I shall see in his hands the print of the nails, and put my finger into the print of the nails, and thrust my hand into his side, I will not believe.” What would they need nails for on a tree? His hands and feet were nailed to a cross, and he hung there for hours, lynched slowly. And they mocked him: “If thou be the Son of God, come down from the cross.” A man hanging by the neck from a tree could not be answering questions; he would be choking to death. So Peter called the crucifixion hanging on a tree, and the two men beside him were lynched too.

It is ironic: the same way the white man lynched us in slavery and into the 60s is the same way our King was killed. That is why Galatians 3:13 matters: “Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. Christ was hanged on a tree under the same curse as his people.

precepts.label: Deuteronomy 21:23
precepts.why:
Hanging was our punishment too, in the law, for the wicked: “And if a man have committed a sin worthy of death, and he be to be put to death, and thou hang him on a tree:” “His body shall not remain all night upon the tree, but thou shalt in any wise bury him that day; (for he that is hanged is accursed of God;) that thy land be not defiled”.

That is what Paul quotes in Galatians 3:13: “Christ hath redeemed us from the curse of the law, being made a curse for us: for it is written, Cursed is every one that hangeth on a tree”. The curse of the law means its condemnation; being made a curse means being put to death for us, a sacrifice.

So what happened to our people? We were hanged on trees, because we went under the curses. Christ went under the curses of Deuteronomy 28 along with us, and we are under the curses too. He that is hanged is accursed of God: Christ was hanged on a tree, and so were we. The King and his children were hanged.

And the pattern keeps turning, like a ring. In Egypt, when Moses said, let my people go to serve God, Pharaoh called us idle and took away the straw but kept the tale of bricks, with a quota of 2,000 bricks; the records name Yupa son of Uriah, a Hebrew, 370 short. Here it was a quota of 200 or 500 pounds of cotton. The officers set over us, the black elites, pastors and politicians in the white man's pocket, turned on Moses and Aaron for making Pharaoh hate them. It is the same curse, the same judgment, until Christ, who bore the curse, redeems us from it.
